1.w: Be imitators of me, as I also [am] of Christ.

2.w: Now I commend you⁺ because you⁺ have remembered me in all things, and you⁺ hold fast the traditions just as I delivered [them] to you⁺.

3.w: But I want you⁺ to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman [is] the man, and the head of Christ [is] God.

4.w: Every man praying or prophesying having [anything] on [his] head dishonors his head.

5.w: And every woman praying or prophesying with the head uncovered dishonors her head; for it is one and the same with having been shaven.

6.w: For if a woman does not cover her head, also let her be shorn. And if [it is] shameful to a woman to be shorn or to be shaven, let her cover her head.

7.w: For indeed a man ought not to cover the head, being the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

8.w: For man is not of woman, but woman of man.

9.w: For also man was not created because of the woman, but woman because of the man.

10.w: Because of this, the woman ought to have authority on the head, because of the angels.

11.w: However, neither [is] woman apart from man, nor man apart from woman in the Lord.

12.w: For just as the woman [is] of the man, so also the man [is] through the woman. And all things [are] of God.

13.w: Judge in yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God uncovered?

14.w: Does not even nature itself teach you⁺ that indeed if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,

15.w: but if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her? For the long hair instead of a covering is given to her.

16.w: Now if anyone thinks to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.

17.w: Now in this instructing, I do not praise [you], because not for the better, but for the worse, do you⁺ come together.

18.w: For first indeed, [on] your⁺ coming together in an assembly, I hear there to be divisions among you⁺, and in part I believe it.

19.w: For also it is necessary for there to be factions among you⁺, so that also the ones approved should become evident among you⁺.

20.w: Therefore, [on] your⁺ coming together in the same [place], it is not to eat the Lord’s supper.

21.w: For in eating, each takes first [his] own supper. And indeed this one is hungry, but that one is drunk.

22.w: What! Have you⁺ no houses in which to eat and to drink? Or do you⁺ despise the church of God and put to shame those not having? What shall I say to you⁺? Shall I praise you⁺? In this I do not praise [you]!

23.w: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you⁺, that the Lord Jesus, in the night in which He was delivered up, took bread,

24.w: and having given thanks, He broke [it] and said, “This is My body, which [is] for you⁺; do this to the remembrance of Me.”

25.w: Likewise also the cup after having supped, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you⁺ may drink [it], to the remembrance of Me.”

26.w: For as often as you⁺ may eat this bread and may drink the cup, you⁺ proclaim the death of the Lord until He should come.

27.w: Therefore, whoever may eat the bread or may drink the cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord.

28.w: But let a man examine himself, and thus let him eat of the bread, and let him drink of the cup.

29.w: For the one eating and drinking, not discerning the body, eats and drinks judgment on himself.

30.w: Because of this, many [are] weak and sick among you⁺, and many are fallen asleep.

31.w: For if we were discerning of ourselves, we would not be being judged.

32.w: But being judged by the Lord, we are disciplined, so that we should not be condemned with the world.

33.w: So then, my brothers, [in] coming together in order to eat, wait for one another.

34.w: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you⁺ may not come together for judgment; and I will prescribe the other things as soon as I shall come.
